findings.title: This decodes a JWT without verifying its signature, so the claims are client-controlled and any identity in them is self-asserted

evidence.summary: This decodes a JWT without verifying its signature, so the claims are client-controlled and any identity in them is self-asserted.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Call jwt.decode with the key and algorithms set, and leave verification on. If a test needs an unverified decode, keep that in the test, not in the request path.
remediation.root_cause_hint: Signature verification was switched off, usually to get past an error during development.

findings.title: A shell command is built from a request value

evidence.summary: A shell command is built from a request value. The shell interprets metacharacters, so a caller can append their own command.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Drop shell=True and pass a list of arguments, for example subprocess.run(["convert", src, dst], check=True), and validate the value against an allowlist.
remediation.root_cause_hint: shell=True hands the assembled string to a shell, which parses the request value as syntax.

findings.title: A SQL statement is built with string formatting from a request value

evidence.summary: A SQL statement is built with string formatting from a request value. The value becomes part of the statement, so a caller controls the query.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Pass the value as a bound parameter instead, for example cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = %s", (order_id,)), or use the ORM's filter API. Note that the comma matters: passing a tuple is parameterization, while % formatting is not.
remediation.root_cause_hint: The query is assembled with f-strings, % or .format(), so the value is interpolated into the statement's syntax.

findings.title: Debug mode is enabled

evidence.summary: Debug mode is enabled. In Flask this exposes an interactive console on error pages, which allows code execution; in Django it returns settings and query contents in error responses.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Drive this from configuration and default it off, for example debug=os.environ.get("FLASK_DEBUG") == "1". The interactive debugger must never be reachable on a deployed instance.
remediation.root_cause_hint: A development convenience is set unconditionally rather than from the environment.

findings.title: The whole request body is written into a record

evidence.summary: The whole request body is written into a record. A caller can set any field the model accepts, including ones the UI never exposes, such as role, is_admin, owner_id or balance.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Pick the permitted fields explicitly before writing, for example order = {"item": payload["item"]}, and never pass the request body or a permissive model's dump straight into an update or create call.
remediation.root_cause_hint: The write path trusts the shape of the request body instead of selecting the fields it is willing to accept.

findings.title: A password is being hashed with a general-purpose digest

evidence.summary: A password is being hashed with a general-purpose digest. These are built to be fast, which is the opposite of what password storage needs: an attacker with the hash list can try candidates at enormous rates.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Use a password hashing function with a work factor, such as argon2id, scrypt or bcrypt, through a library that salts each password. Migrate existing hashes by re-hashing on next successful login.
remediation.root_cause_hint: A hash function was chosen for availability rather than for deliberate slowness and per-password salting.

findings.title: A security-relevant value is being generated from a non-cryptographic random source

evidence.summary: A security-relevant value is being generated from a non-cryptographic random source. These generators are seeded predictably and their output can be reproduced, so the token can be guessed.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Generate the value with a cryptographic source, for example crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("hex") or secrets.token_urlsafe(32).
remediation.root_cause_hint: The convenient random function was used where a cryptographic one is required.

findings.title: This view looks up a record by an identifier taken from the request URL without scoping the query to the current user

evidence.summary: This view looks up a record by an identifier taken from the request URL without scoping the query to the current user. Any authenticated caller can read another user's record by changing the id.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Filter the query by the current user as well as the id, for example Order.query.filter_by(id=order_id, user_id=current_user.id) .first_or_404(), so a record belonging to someone else is simply not found.
remediation.root_cause_hint: The query is keyed only on a path parameter, so the record's owner is never part of the lookup.

findings.title: The response reflects the request's Origin header while allowing credentials, which permits any site to make credentialed calls to this API on a user's behalf

evidence.summary: The response reflects the request's Origin header while allowing credentials, which permits any site to make credentialed calls to this API on a user's behalf.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Configure an explicit list of allowed origins, for example with flask-cors' origins parameter, and do not echo the Origin header.
remediation.root_cause_hint: The allowed origin is taken from the request instead of from configuration.

findings.title: The server fetches a caller-supplied URL, so requests originate from inside your network and can reach internal services and instance metadata

evidence.summary: The server fetches a caller-supplied URL, so requests originate from inside your network and can reach internal services and instance metadata.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Restrict fetches to an allowlist of hosts, resolve the name and reject private, loopback and link-local addresses, and re-check on every redirect.
remediation.root_cause_hint: The URL is taken from the request and fetched without resolving and checking the destination address.

findings.title: A filesystem path is built from a request value without being confined to an intended directory, so a caller can traverse out of it

evidence.summary: A filesystem path is built from a request value without being confined to an intended directory, so a caller can traverse out of it.

steps: The flagged pattern is the one described in the evidence summary.

remediation.guidance: Resolve the path and confirm it is still under the intended root, for example with Path(root).joinpath(name).resolve() followed by an is_relative_to(root) check, or use send_from_directory, which performs that check for you.
remediation.root_cause_hint: os.path.join with an absolute or dot-dot segment discards the base directory entirely.

findings.title: pyjwt 1.7.1 has a known vulnerability (PYSEC-2026-120)

evidence.summary: pyjwt 1.7.1 is affected by PYSEC-2026-120, GHSA-752w-5fwx-jx9f. PyJWT is a JSON Web Token implementation in Python. Prior to 2.12.0, PyJWT does not validate the crit (Critical) Header Parameter defined in RFC 7515 §4.1.11. When a JWS token contains a crit array listing extensions that PyJWT does not understand, the library accepts the token instead of rejecting it. This violates the MUST requirement in the RFC. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.12.0.

remediation.guidance: Upgrade pyjwt to 2.12.0, then re-resolve the lockfile.
